side_evidence: 0x8403C4 (SEC2 PLM, DMEM 0x8401c0/c4 real port, first 8 KiB all zero)

decoding_rules: FEAT_READOUT_1 field offsets are NON-contiguous: 0,3,7,10,13,16,19,22,28 (bit6 and bits 27:25 are gaps). The naive 'nine contiguous 3-bit fields' decoder used for Ampere/Ada is WRONG here and will misdecode 0x00c36180.

On Blackwell, selector value 3 measures as ~half rate (not the 1/8 the public ctrl2080gr.h enum implies for older chips). Measured: FMLA32=3 gives ~48.33 TFLOPS at stock 180W vs ~86.27 TFLOPS theoretical ceiling, ~1.79x gap.
FUSE_EN_SW_OVERRIDE=0 does NOT mean unclamped -- it only governs CTRL_OPT floorsweep, not the rate selector. Both the 170HX and 4090 unlocked successfully while this fuse was 0.
FUSE_SS_PLM (0x8200FC) is NOT the live write gate -- FEAT_OVR_PLM (0x823804) is. FLR resets FUSE_SS_PLM to 0x80842bcf (transiently equal to FEAT_OVR_PLM) before it re-locks to 0xfffffbff.

Nonzero SS0/SS1 does NOT mean unlocked. Enable bits (nibble bit 3) are clear at factory default; a nonzero word is pre-driver shadow state that can vary boot-to-boot but is stable within one boot. The only valid unlock judgement is SS0==0x88888888 && SS1==0x8.

architecture_fact.ada_ampere_chain: ... -> SEC2 (signed Booter, has the exploitable DMA-overflow-into-stack bug) -> GSP-RM
architecture_fact.blackwell_chain: FSP (ROM, PL3) -> GSP BootROM (ROM, PL3) -> FMC (host-supplied, signed+encrypted, PL3) -> GSP-RM (PL2)
architecture_fact.implication: No SEC2 stage exists on Blackwell. The vulnerability class that broke Turing/Ampere/Ada (signed Booter stack overflow -> ROP -> privileged PLM write) has no equivalent component to target.
